slides.title: It's usually the network, not VoIP
slides.body: Choppy or robotic sound happens when bits of your voice arrive late or get lost on the way. The technology isn't the problem.

slides.title: Busy Wi-Fi squeezes your calls
slides.body: Crowded Wi-Fi, or a big upload running in the background, competes with your voice. A desk phone on a cable avoids that.

slides.title: Calls should get priority
slides.body: A properly set-up router puts voice first (it's called QoS), so a big download never cuts into a conversation.

caption:
"VoIP sounds robotic." Does it? 🤖📞

A lot of people expect internet calls to be choppy, delayed or robotic. When that happens, it's almost always the network, not VoIP itself: bits of your voice arrive late or get lost on the way.

The usual culprits:
✅ Crowded Wi-Fi or a big upload running in the background
✅ A router that doesn't give voice priority (QoS)
✅ Phones on Wi-Fi when a cable would do
